title: Investigation into Montfort School Bullying Incident and Standardising Punishment Framework for School Bullying Cases
what_it_is: Investigation into Montfort School Bullying Incident and Standardising Punishment Framework for School Bullying Cases

sections.label: Questions on school bullying
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about zero tolerance, a centralised investigation unit, standardised punishment, the Montfort Secondary School case, and recourse for victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will be minded to adopt a clear zero-tolerance stance towards bullying in our schools; (b) whether the Ministry will be minded to (i) set up a centralised investigation unit and (ii) standardise and centrally administer a framework for punishment and rehabilitation to deal with egregious cases of bullying in our schools; and (c) if not, why not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has launched an investigation into the bullying case at Montfort Secondary School; and (b) if so, what is the outcome of the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education what actions can the school take and what can the Ministry provide as a recourse to victims and their families if the bullying behaviour of a student continues even after police reports have been filed, the school's leadership informed and the bully’s parents notified.

sections.label: MOE statements on bullying
sections.summary: MOE issued a media statement on 3 March 2025 about the Montfort Secondary School fighting incident, and detailed its bullying processes on 14 October 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: On the Monfort Secondary School fighting incident, the Ministry of Education (MOE) issued a media statement on 3 March 2025 about the outcome of the school’s investigations and the actions taken by the school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For Members who asked about MOE’s processes for handling bullying incidents, these have been comprehensively detailed in MOE’s Parliamentary response on 14 October 2024.

sections.label: School investigation and disciplinary actions
sections.summary: Schools conduct thorough investigations when incidents are reported, then decide on disciplinary and rehabilitative actions, with legal consequences for serious cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: When an incident is reported, the school will conduct thorough investigations to understand the facts before deciding on the appropriate course of action – which could include both disciplinary and rehabilitative actions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For serious cases, perpetrators will face legal consequences in accordance with the law.

sections.label: Bystanders and recordings punished
sections.summary: Bystanders and those who recorded and shared the incident online will be called out, counselled and punished if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Bystanders and those who recorded the incident and shared the recordings online will also be called out, counselled and punished if necessary.
